spans.text: Reviewing a change to Super's own files — 2026-09-12
Status: a design, for a ruling. Nothing here is built.
Super cannot review a complete change to its own larger source files. This is the record of what actually stops it, the two ways to fix it, and the one change that cannot itself go through review.
Submitting the second held dogfood proposal (seven files) against this repository on 2026-09-12 produced two refusals from two different layers:
7 files   frame of 336202 bytes exceeds the 262144 byte limit 2 files   attempt-fields-invalid — "A change set needs two to four complete, valid file replacements."

One change set is most of an authority store, and every unrelated mutation — opening a workspace, creating a plan, closing a worker — rewrites those bytes. A four-file set of the files above would be roughly 214 KB of text, making the store about ten times its present size, rewritten on every world mutation.

This is not "remove the limits". It is "put each limit on the thing it is about".

"A change set needs two to four complete, valid file replacements"
— a sentence about counting, when the count was two. A person reads it and counts their files.
Four distinct refusals, each naming what failed and, where it applies, which file:
fewer than the minimum or more than the maximum members
the count given, and the bounds
one member's current or proposed content exceeds the per-file cap
the path, which side, the size, the cap
the members together exceed the per-set cap
not valid text, a NUL byte, a digest that disagrees with its bytes, or content that was never uploaded
the path and which of those
None of them discloses file contents back to the caller.
A change that adds staged upload cannot be submitted through staged upload, and the running desktop is the thing being changed. So exactly one change has to reach
— the command definitions, the content store, the validator and its refusals.
That change should be as small as it can be and should be the last one made this way. Everything after it, including the held repository-label proposal, goes through review.

It is presented as a diff for a ruling before it is applied to the running system, because applying it means replacing the binary Travis's desktop is running and restarting it, which revokes every paired phone session.

nothing publishes a name and the other files do nothing.
